plan.planSummary: S04 implements native Event CRUD + recurring EventSeries, replacing the CiviCRM-sync model. Backend: one inspector-guarded Alembic migration (down_revision=i3j4k5l6m7n8) adding the event_series table + 6 columns to events; ORM models for EventSeries and the expanded Event; 13 new Pydantic schemas (expanding the thin EventResponse); a full paginated CRUD events router with participant sub-resources; a new event_series router with a generate endpoint; an event_generator service holding cadence constants + PHT→UTC generation logic (imported by S16); 2 DynamicSettings helpers; main.py router registration; and comprehensive SQLite test suites. The schema-inversion test must flip (is_active removed from the must-be-absent set, S04 columns asserted present, event_series table asserted to exist) — this is a breaking-test dependency that must land with the model change. Frontend: new typed events service + types, full EventsPage rewrite (strip Sync/CiviCRM, add filter pills, badges, pagination), new EventDetailPage + ParticipantGrid, EventSeriesPage + EventFormDrawer + EventTypeBadge/SessionTimeBadge, App.tsx routes, and BottomNav admin link. Critical ordering: F01/F02 (migration+models) gate everything; F02 must land with P01 (test flip) or the suite goes red; F06 (service) gates F05; F03/P03 (schemas) gate routers; frontend F09 (types/service) gates all UI tasks.

featureTasks.name: S04-F01: Alembic migration — event_series table + events column additions
featureTasks.acceptanceCriteria: (a) New file backend/alembic/versions/<rev>_s04_event_series_and_event_columns.py exists with revision set and down_revision='i3j4k5l6m7n8'. (b) Static inspection passes: op.create_table('event_series') textually appears BEFORE op.add_column('events','recurring_series_id'); ondelete='SET NULL' present on the FK; is_active column added with server_default=sa.true() (DEFAULT TRUE); both indexes ix_events_event_type and ix_events_occurrence_date created; a backfill UPDATE events SET occurrence_date=DATE(start_at) present; downgrade drops the 6 events columns then drop_table('event_series'). (c) Every op guarded by inspector checks (has_table / column-name list) so re-run is idempotent. (d) Postgres-gated round-trip test backend/tests/test_s04_migration_content.py decorated @pytest.mark.skipif(not is_postgres(), reason='migration CI only') passes; on SQLite it is collected as a skip. (e) Full SQLite suite stays GREEN (create_all builds schema, migration DDL not exercised). (f) ruff check app passes.
featureTasks.engineerNotes: Mirror the exact structure of i3j4k5l6m7n8_s07_face_enrollment_and_samples.py: `from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB as PG_JSONB`, `_JSONB = sa.JSON().with_variant(PG_JSONB(), 'postgresql')`. event_series.cadence uses _JSONB nullable=False with server_default sa.text("'{}'::jsonb") — NOTE the existing photo_ingest_batches migration uses '[]'::jsonb which works because batch_alter is not involved; the ::jsonb cast is Postgres-only and is fine since the migration only runs on Postgres in CI. Inspector-guard pattern from h1i2j3k4l5m6: `bind=op.get_bind(); insp=sa_inspect(bind)`; guard table with `if 'event_series' not in insp.get_table_names()`; guard columns with `cols=[c['name'] for c in insp.get_columns('events')]; if 'event_type' not in cols`. Order is load-bearing: create event_series FIRST, then add events.recurring_series_id (FK references it). is_active: add with `sa.Column('is_active', sa.Boolean(), nullable=False, server_default=sa.true())` — do NOT add anything heavier (RISK: forced table rewrite). For ix_events_occurrence_date DESC, use postgresql_ops={'occurrence_date':'DESC'} on op.create_index — safe because migration is Postgres-only. event_type add: `nullable=False, server_default=sa.text("'Event'")`. Backfill: `op.execute("UPDATE events SET occurrence_date = DATE(start_at) WHERE start_at IS NOT NULL")` — irreversible (RISK noted). For is_postgres() helper, check backend/tests for an existing one (other migration tests use it) and import it; if none exists add a small local helper reading the DATABASE_URL dialect.

featureTasks.name: S04-F02: ORM Models — EventSeries + Event column additions
featureTasks.acceptanceCriteria: (a) EventSeries model exists in models.py with id, title String(255), event_type String(50), session_time String(20) nullable, cadence using JSONB (the module-level JSON().with_variant alias) nullable=False default=dict, default_location String(255) nullable, is_active Boolean default=True, created_at DateTime default=utc_now. (b) Event model gains event_type String(50) nullable=False default='Event', session_time String(20) nullable, occurrence_date Date nullable, recurring_series_id Integer FK→event_series.id ondelete='SET NULL' nullable, is_active Boolean default=True, location String(255) nullable. (c) Event.__table_args__ adds Index('ix_events_event_type','event_type') and Index('ix_events_occurrence_date','occurrence_date') alongside the existing two indexes. (d) SQLite suite GREEN: create_all builds the full schema; sample_event fixture still inserts (event_type/is_active have Python defaults). (e) ruff check app passes.
featureTasks.engineerNotes: EventSeries MUST be declared BEFORE Event so the string FK 'event_series.id' resolves at mapper configuration (RISK: SQLAlchemy table order for string FK refs). Reuse the module-level JSONB alias already at models.py line 25 — do NOT redefine. Use Date (already imported) for occurrence_date. FK pattern: `mapped_column(Integer, ForeignKey('event_series.id', ondelete='SET NULL'), nullable=True)`. Index is already imported. The cadence default=dict mirrors Contact.custom_data. Do NOT add server_default in the model for is_active (Python-side default only, per spec — migration owns the DDL server_default). This task is tightly coupled to S04-P01: applying F02 without P01 turns test_schema_inversion.py::test_events_has_no_s04_columns RED — land them together.

(b) All 13 schema classes present: EventCreate, EventUpdate, ParticipantCounts, EventResponse (expanded), EventDetailResponse (=EventResponse + participant_counts: ParticipantCounts), PaginatedEventResponse, EventSeriesCreate, EventSeriesUpdate, EventSeriesResponse, EventParticipantItem (with contact_display_name computed field), ParticipantListResponse, ParticipantManualAdd, ParticipantStatusUpdate. All new event fields must be Optional with defaults so the expanded EventResponse remains backward compatible for serialization (RISK: GET /events 500 if model columns absent — mitigated because F02 lands first). contact_display_name on EventParticipantItem: use @computed_field or accept it as a plain field the router populates from the Contact join (router builds the dict, so a plain `contact_display_name: str` is simplest given the contact_service pattern that builds dicts). AC3 invalid event_type → 422. AC4 soft-deleted event hidden from default GET /events, visible with ?is_active=false. AC5 soft-delete of the active event → 200 with a warning in body. AC7 POST /events/{id}/participants → 201 source='manual'; duplicate (event_id,contact_id) → 409. AC8 PATCH /events/{id}/participants/{pid}/status updates status. AC9 POST /events/set-active for missing event → 404 detail exactly 'Event {id} not found.'. AC10 25 events, page_size=20 → 20 items + total=25. test_volunteer_cannot_create_event → 403. GET /events/{id} returns EventDetailResponse with participant_counts from the service. ruff check app passes.
featureTasks.engineerNotes: Route ORDER is load-bearing: keep /active-event-id and /set-active registered BEFORE the new /events/{id} routes or FastAPI shadows them. Replace list_events with paginated GET '' supporting type→event_type, date_from, date_to, series_id, is_active (default True), page, page_size (default 20, cap 200) returning PaginatedEventResponse. POST /events: require_admin, auto-set occurrence_date=start_at.date() when omitted, validate session_time only allowed when event_type=='Sunday Celebration' else 422, then `await audit_svc.record(db, actor_id=int(user['sub']), action='event.create', entity='event', entity_id=ev.id, before=None, after={...})` and db.commit(). Import audit as `from app.services import audit as audit_svc`. Reads + participant writes use require_volunteer; event writes/delete use require_admin. participant_counts come from event_generator.get_event_participant_counts (F06) — import lazily or top-level after F06 lands. 409 handling: `from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError`, wrap participant insert, on IntegrityError → HTTPException(409). featureTasks.name: S04-F06: event_generator.py service — cadence constants + generation logic
featureTasks.acceptanceCriteria: Module-level constants exactly: SUNDAY_CRON=={'day_of_week':'fri','hour':18,'minute':0}; POWERHOUSE_CRON=={'day_of_week':'wed','hour':8,'minute':0}; plus EOW_RECOMPUTE_CRON, EOM_RECOMPUTE_CRON, NOTIFIER_CRONS per spec §4.2. get_event_participant_counts(event_id, db)→{unique_count:0,total_count:0} for an event with no participants. generate_sunday_events(series_id, db, target_date=None) creates 3 events whose naive-UTC start_at are 00:00 (8AM PHT), 02:00 (10AM PHT), 07:00 (3PM PHT) on the target date — asserted by test_generate_sunday_events_pht_utc. generate_powerhouse_event(series_id, db, target_date=None) creates one Powerhouse event start_at=target+13h, and a second call with the same date returns None (idempotent). generate_series_occurrence(series_id, db, target_date)→{created,skipped,events} dispatching on series.event_type. config.DynamicSettings.get_sunday_series_id() and get_powerhouse_series_id() return None by default.
featureTasks.engineerNotes: Function signatures are FROZEN — S16 imports SUNDAY_CRON, POWERHOUSE_CRON, generate_sunday_events, generate_powerhouse_event from this module. PHT=UTC+8, store naive UTC (utc_now convention). Compute UTC start_at by subtracting the PHT offset: 8AM PHT → date+timedelta(hours=0); 10AM PHT → hours=2; 3PM PHT → hours=7; Powerhouse 9PM PHT → hours=13 (these are PHT_hour-8). Idempotency is query-before-insert (NOT a DB unique constraint, per spec §4.3): before inserting check existence on (occurrence_date, event_type, session_time, recurring_series_id); count existing as 'skipped'. Use async SQLAlchemy COUNT for participant counts: unique_count=COUNT(DISTINCT contact_id), total_count=COUNT(*) on participants WHERE event_id=. JSON cadence reads work on SQLite as plain JSON. Add config helpers following get_active_event_id() at config.py line 145 — same None-coercion logic. NOTE F05 depends on this, so build this first.

plan.risks: 1. BREAKING TEST (must co-land): S04-F02 adds the S04 columns to the Event ORM, which immediately fails test_schema_inversion.py::test_events_has_no_s04_columns unless S04-P01 lands in the same change. Sequence F01→F02+P01 atomically. 2. EventResponse expansion (F03/P03) requires the Event columns to exist in models.py first; applying schemas before models risks 500s on GET /events serialization. F02 must precede F03/P03. 3. Migration down_revision='i3j4k5l6m7n8' makes S04 chain AFTER S07 (counterintuitive but spec-mandated) — do not 'fix' it. 4. is_active on events must use server_default=sa.true() only; anything heavier forces a Postgres table rewrite. 5. occurrence_date backfill UPDATE is irreversible by downgrade (data loss on rollback) — acceptable, but document it. 6. event_series must be created before events.recurring_series_id in the migration (FK target). 7. ix_events_occurrence_date DESC uses postgresql_ops — fine because the migration is Postgres-only/CI-gated; the SQLite test path uses create_all from ORM (plain index) and never runs the migration. 8. PHT→UTC offsets are hardcoded raw timedelta math (no tz lib): 8AM=00:00, 10AM=02:00, 3PM=07:00, 9PM=13:00 UTC — a single wrong constant fails generation tests and S16 schedulers. 9. event_generator function signatures are an external contract for S16 — freeze them. 10. Idempotency is query-before-insert, NOT a DB unique constraint (spec §4.3). 11. ContactPickerModal returns a Member object and queries /members; F11 must adapt it for participant add (read .contact_id) rather than assuming an Event-participant shape. 12. components/events/ directory does not exist — first frontend events task must create it. 13. audit_svc.record requires actor_id=int(user['sub']) (sub is a string in the JWT claims) — passing the raw string will fail the integer FK. 14. 409 on duplicate participant requires catching sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError specifically against uq_participant_event_contact. 15. Route order in events.py: /active-event-id and /set-active must stay registered before /events/{id} to avoid path shadowing. 16. P04 is a silent behavior change — the event_type filter on /members/{id}/attendance becomes active once Event.event_type exists; verify existing attendance tests still pass.

recon.stack: Backend: Python/FastAPI (async), SQLAlchemy 2.x (async ORM with Mapped/mapped_column), Alembic for migrations, Pydantic v2 (schemas), pytest-asyncio (asyncio_mode=auto), SQLite via aiosqlite for tests, PostgreSQL for production. Frontend: React 18 + TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Query v5, Axios, Zustand (auth/task stores), Tailwind CSS v3, Lucide React icons, Sonner for toasts, React Router v6, Vitest + Testing Library for frontend tests.

recon.patterns:
1. Auth: HTTPBearer dependency via require_admin/require_volunteer in dependencies.py. Role check: user['role'] == 'admin'. Current user dict has {sub, email, name, role}.

2. Async DB sessions: All routers use `db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)`. Queries use `await db.execute(select(...))` then `.scalars().all()` or `.scalar_one_or_none()`. Commits done explicitly with `await db.commit()`.

3. Error handling: HTTPException(status_code=..., detail='...'). IntegrityError must be imported from sqlalchemy.exc for 409 handling.

4. ORM model pattern: Uses SQLAlchemy 2.x Mapped/mapped_column declarative style. FK pattern: `mapped_column(Integer, ForeignKey('table.id', ondelete='SET NULL'), nullable=True)`. Index in __table_args__ tuple. JSONB cross-dialect: `JSON().with_variant(_PG_JSONB, 'postgresql')` (already imported as JSONB in models.py).

5. Audit logging: `from app.services import audit as audit_svc` then `await audit_svc.record(db, actor_id=user['sub'], action='entity.verb', entity='entity_name', entity_id=id, before={...}, after={...})`. Caller commits.

6. Pydantic schemas: Use `model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)` for ORM-mapped schemas. Optional fields with `Optional[X] = None`. Literal types for constrained strings.

7. Migration pattern (inspector-guarded): `bind = op.get_bind(); insp = sa_inspect(bind); if 'tablename' not in insp.get_table_names(): op.create_table(...)`. Column guard: `cols = [c['name'] for c in insp.get_columns('tablename')]; if 'colname' not in cols: op.add_column(...)`.

8. JSONB in migrations: `_JSONB = sa.JSON().with_variant(PG_JSONB(), 'postgresql')` at top of migration file. Server defaults use `sa.text("'{}'::jsonb")` for Postgres but need to be SQLite-safe (plain `'{}'` without ::jsonb cast).

9. Frontend API calls: `api.get('/endpoint', {params: {...}}).then(r => r.data)`. Service files export typed functions using the shared `api` axios instance from services/api.ts.

10. TanStack Query keys: Arrays like `['events', {type, dateFrom, page}]`. Invalidation uses `queryClient.invalidateQueries({queryKey: ['events']})`.

11. Frontend test pattern: vi.mock for service modules, useAuthStore mocked as `vi.fn((selector) => selector({isAdmin: false}))`. Render wrapped in QueryClientProvider + MemoryRouter. waitFor for async assertions.

12. Naming conventions: Backend snake_case throughout. Frontend camelCase for variables/functions, PascalCase for components/types. File names: backend uses underscores (event_series.py), frontend uses PascalCase (EventSeriesPage.tsx) or camelCase (events.ts for services).

13. Router registration in main.py: `app.include_router(router, dependencies=[Depends(check_setup_complete)])`. Import pattern: `from app.routers import event_series as event_series_router`.

14. Soft delete pattern: Set is_active=False rather than DELETE. The set_active_event endpoint pattern shows use of db.get(Model, id) for single-row fetches.

15. Pagination pattern: Backend returns {total, page, page_size, items}. Frontend uses Pagination component from components/ui/Pagination.tsx with {page, pageSize, total, onPageChange, onPageSizeChange} props.
recon.risks:
1. BREAKING CHANGE — test_schema_inversion.py test_events_has_no_s04_columns: Currently asserts that event_type, session_time, occurrence_date, recurring_series_id, and location are ABSENT from events. S04-F02 adds them, so this test will fail unless S04-P01 is applied first (or concurrently). The spec says to flip the assertion. Also, the existing test at line 110-112 (test_events_columns) only requires the 6 core columns — it will still pass after S04-F02 since it uses subset-check logic.

2. BREAKING CHANGE — EventResponse schema: The existing GET /events returns EventResponse with only {id, title, start_at, end_at}. S04-P03 expands it with 6 new fields. Any frontend code reading EventResponse will see extra fields (backward-compatible for JSON consumers), but the ORM-to-schema serialization requires the new Event columns to exist in models.py BEFORE the expanded schema is applied. If models.py and schemas.py changes are applied independently, a partial state could cause 500 errors on GET /events.

3. conftest.py sample_event fixture (line 276-286): Currently creates minimal Event per CN-16 comment. After S04-F02 adds NOT NULL DEFAULT columns to Event ORM, the fixture remains valid because event_type has a default ('Event') and is_active defaults to True. No fixture changes needed, but verify carefully.

4. Alembic migration order risk: The new S04 migration sets down_revision='i3j4k5l6m7n8' (S07 head). This means S04 depends on S07 in the migration chain, which is counterintuitive (S04 < S07 semantically). This is the specified behavior and must be followed exactly.

5. is_active NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE on events: Spec warns explicitly 'Do NOT add server_default on is_active beyond DEFAULT TRUE (no forced table rewrite)'. In the migration, use server_default=sa.true() for the add_column call. The ORM model uses mapped_column(Boolean, default=True) (Python-side only). On Postgres, adding a NOT NULL column with a server_default does not require a table rewrite, but omitting server_default would require one (PostgreSQL 11+ can handle it with DEFAULT, older cannot without rewrite).

6. Occurrence_date backfill: The migration must run UPDATE events SET occurrence_date = DATE(start_at) WHERE start_at IS NOT NULL. This is a data mutation in upgrade() that is irreversible by downgrade() (downgrade drops the column, data is lost).

7. recurring_series_id FK ON DELETE SET NULL: In the migration, event_series must be created BEFORE recurring_series_id is added to events (FK reference). The spec calls this out explicitly: 'create_table event_series before add_column for recurring_series_id'.

8. ContactPickerModal reuse (S04-F11): The existing ContactPickerModal (frontend/src/components/tasks/ContactPickerModal.tsx) uses Member type and calls /members endpoint. For participant add in EventDetailPage, this modal needs to either be reused as-is or a new variant created. The existing modal interface returns Member objects. This may need adaptation.

9. event_generator.py PHT-to-UTC conversion: The service generates events at specific Philippine time (PHT = UTC+8). 8AM PHT = 00:00 UTC, 10AM PHT = 02:00 UTC, 3PM PHT = 07:00 UTC, 9PM PHT = 13:00 UTC. These hardcoded offsets must be precisely correct. No timezone library dependency is mentioned — raw timedelta arithmetic is expected.

10. Frontend components/events/ directory: Does not exist yet. All 4 new component files (EventFormDrawer, ParticipantGrid, EventTypeBadge, SessionTimeBadge) require creating this directory.

11. contact_service.py hasattr guard (lines 507-555): The guard `hasattr(Event, 'event_type')` will evaluate to True once S04-F02 lands, meaning the event_type filter in GET /members/{id}/attendance will become active. This is desired behavior per S04-P04 but is a silent behavior change to an existing endpoint.

12. Idempotency of migration indexes: The spec requires ix_events_occurrence_date to be DESC. Alembic's create_index supports postgresql_ops={'occurrence_date': 'DESC'} or column descriptor with desc(). On SQLite (test path), DESC indexes are not supported the same way — need to handle with conditional or plain index for SQLite.

13. S04-F08 tests run under SQLite: The test suite uses SQLite via aiosqlite. The event_generator service uses async SQLAlchemy queries; these must be compatible with SQLite. The JSON cadence column uses JSON().with_variant(JSONB, 'postgresql') which works on SQLite as plain JSON.

14. Potential 409 conflict handling in POST /events/{id}/participants: The spec requires catching IntegrityError for duplicate (event_id, contact_id) which violates the unique constraint uq_participant_event_contact. The router must import and catch sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError specifically.

15. AdminRoute vs ProtectedRoute for EventSeriesPage: EventSeriesPage should use AdminRoute (it's an admin-only page). EventDetailPage uses ProtectedRoute (volunteer-accessible). This mirrors the existing pattern in App.tsx.
